utterances.text: Page 6, last paragraph: "About three months before the conflict, Pican Juro", that is a person's name, "had carried some hay for us. I had gone to the Pican cafe to pay him. Juro's mother, Andja, told me that something is going to happen. There are meetings in front of my stable. They are trying to hide it from me but I know that something is going on. Andja told me they were going to cleanse Muslim people from Ahmici."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That will be all, Mr. President. We have completed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will turn to the Prosecutor again, who perhaps might have some clarifications or other questions, but only in relation to the cross-examination, please. Clarifications, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Ahmic, I am now going to turn to my colleagues to know whether they would like to ask you some additional questions. We will start with Judge Riad. Judge Riad, have you any questions you wish to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Ms. Fatima Ahmic, you just said a few seconds ago that Pican Juro said that they are going to cleanse the Muslims from Ahmici. When was that exactly before the events, before they started coming to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in August, I do not know what date it was. This Juro Pican was bringing me hay from my fields and he brought in the hay and my husband wanted to pay and he said, "Hasim, do not give me any money, just buy me some cigarettes", that is what he said. "I bring money to my wife, she spends it on other things and I do not have anything to smoke". Then my husband said, "Fatima, take this and give it to Juro, Fahran and I are going out in the field". That is what happened. He said, "five packs of cigarettes", and my son Fahrudin said, "mama, this is not enough, I am giving two packs too, let it be seven packs of cigarettes". I came in front of Juro's house, Juro was sitting in a chair and grinding coffee and he said, "ah, Hasimovica" -- you know, my husband's name was Hasim, so they called me Hasimovica. He said, "you are just in time for coffee", and I said, "thank you, but I have just had coffee at home". I said, "I am going to come and see your mother because I hear she has been sick". We are from Busovaca, all of us, you know, from one municipality, so we always called each other neighbour. She got up immediately, Andja, to make more coffee, and I said, "no thank you, Andja, I had coffee at home just before I left", and she said, "it is good that you came, Hasimovica. Hasimovica, Hasimovica, you will not believe the things I have to tell you. In front of this stable of mine, this is where they come and they have meetings, and I was wondering what was happening, and one evening, I went there and I was eavesdropping, I wanted to hear what they were saying. Dear Hasimovica, people are going to be cleansed from here, it seems they are going to cleanse all the Muslims from here". You know when this meeting of theirs broke up, I called my Juro, my Jozo and their grandson Zeljo and Miso, the son, and this is what I told them, I said, "what have you been saying that you wanted to cleanse Muslims, dear children?" "Do you know how good Hasim has been to me when your father died?", that is what she said. I am telling you exactly what the woman told me. "When your father died, Hasim would help me, and he came to the store, he said, 'did your Frano die?'" She said, "yes, it happened all of a sudden. Obviously he had a heart attack, and he said, 'if you do not have any money, I am going to give you money for your funeral', so he was very good to me when I was building my house, and he helped me a lot, so you do not have to turn to other people, I am going to give you money for what you need". That is what she told her children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I just want to know, was this exactly at the same time when you heard on television General Blaskic and Mr. Kordic? Was it approximately after it or before it, do you remember, these meetings where they said they will cleanse Muslims from Ahmici, was it almost in the same period as the TV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was when I went to see her, when we were first attacked, you know? I tell you, I cannot remember the date. I just remember, I tell you, it was August, because of the hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it before, because you knew about the television late at night when your son came, Fahrudin came and said he heard on television, was that not right, so these meetings were before the television programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, just a minute. I cannot remember the date exactly. I do not want to lie, I do not want to say a single word that would be false, so I cannot say the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You were surprised to listen, to know this, that there were meetings and they want to cleanse, so that was the first time you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you let me just think about it? You know when I tell you what I told my children when I came back home, if you allow me to tell you about that, it is going to come back to me. Can I tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will not disturb you more with this question. When this cleansing started, was there any discrimination? Did they choose people, you mentioned a lot that Fahrudin went on guard and others went on guard, did they choose particularly those who used to go on guard or was it a common action against everybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Against everybody. Could you please repeat against who? I am here, you know, I cannot concentrate. Please, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the cleansing directed towards special people who were on guard, or who had weapons, or was it against everybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Against everybody, against everybody. They drove us all away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They refused to let you go back, even to look for your things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would not let me take my slippers from in front of the house, they drove me away barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you spoke of the walkie-talkie, I remember you said that Hasim heard the soldiers talking on walkie-talkies. Could he gather whom they were talking to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not Hasim who heard it on the walkie-talkie, I heard it, because I was walking by them and I heard it. They did not tell me, they told my husband something -- I was the first one who came up, because my husband said, "you go and I will catch up with you". I came up to them and their van was standing right next door to Ramiz's house. Three or four of them got out of the van, the van was full of people and one of them was standing in front of there, he took this walkie-talkie and he said, "yes, the action has been successful, they are lying in front of every house like pigs". That is what I heard. Then when my husband came up, then they asked him, "who are you? What is your name?". He told them, and, "what are you carrying in that sack?". He said, "I am taking some clothes for my children, I do not know where they will be". He took two coats and a few shirts and he came by, and that is what they told him. Then they asked him, "where are you going?". He said, "I am going up there, further above Pican's cafe, we are going up there to the store". They said, "go on, go on, we are going to catch up with you and you are going to have coffee with us". He came to me terrified, I was sitting in a corner, you know and he walked up to me and said, "dear Fatima, they are going to come and get me now", and I said, "who?", and he said, "those people who were in the van". I said, "oh no, hopefully not, come on, take off your cap, they will not recognise you". He did take off his cap and he put it down under him. Anto Papic was sitting near me and as Anto Papic got up, he walked out and he said that he would order them to bring children -- the children some milk, Anto went out --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that before, but they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing black uniforms, these people in the van. They were all wearing black uniforms and the people who came to get them at the store, they were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The people who came to get your husband and to get Munib and then you said they were killed, were they also soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms, yes, and they had a lot of weapons, they were fully armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you were in the school in Dubravica, and you said that men came in and chose women and took them out and so on, were they soldiers also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they also had camouflage uniforms on. They were Croats, all of them, they were all Croats, only we civilians were there too and all the rest, all them were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You think it was some kind of a military police where you were staying, this school? It was guarded by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were there, we were their living shield, we were prisoners, we could not go out into the hallway after 6.00 to get some water or to go to the toilet, I beg your pardon. We had some kind of plastic buckets and that is where the children relieved themselves and even the adults too, because they were not allowed to go out, we were all threatened that after 6.00 we were not allowed to go out at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There was a commander called Anto Miskovic and he was kind to you and told you, "do not be afraid while I am here". Was he the commander of the place? Did he have any authority or what was he exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a plain soldier, just a soldier. He was our neighbour, and I knew him and I told him I knew him and I knew the family he is from and he said, "I am ashamed to say who I am and where I am from because of what those fools did down there. I am ashamed of what I am and who I am". Later on, I realised that I knew him, that he was down there by the railway station, but I did not know his name. He came to my yard and I made coffee for him and for this neighbour of mine whose field work he was doing. I said, "I know you from somewhere", and he said, "I know you too, except I am ashamed to say who I am and where I am from because of what those fools did down there". My son was killed and after that I heard the Croats talking about him, they should not have killed him, he was a good man. The women were mourning him too, but nobody protected him. He had so many colleagues and people were talking about war and I said, "my child, something bad is happening, you are going to Vlasik and to Visoko and they have all these weapons in the hills, why are they putting all these weapons up there in the hills, there are no Chetniks among us, why are they putting all these weapons up there?". He said, "mother, you are panicking", and I said, "listen, son, something is in the making, I know it", and that night on television when he saw what was said there and he said, "something is wrong, mother, you are right, everything you have been saying is right", that is what my son told me. Whenever I told him what I noticed, he would always say, "mother, you are panicking too much", he never thought something would happen to him, something would be done by his own colleagues who went to school with him, played music with him. They were friends, and I remember we had Bajram once and there were six carloads of Croats who came to congratulate him on Bajram and then they came to kill him and he did not know that they would kill my poor boy. May dear God in heaven punish them for what they did. It is not only us, it is our entire people, and I heard what this action of theirs was called, "48 hours of ashes", that is to say that after 48 hours, none of us should be left, old or young or men or women or children or old people, they would not spare anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who gave it this name, "48 hours of ashes", do you know? Where did this name come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I just heard about it in the media. In the media. Personally, with my own ears, I heard it in the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Ms. Ahmic, I only have one question to be put to you. You remember you were telling us about Drago Josipovic and Nenad Santic. I think what you said was that Nenad Santic ordered your son to hand over his gun. Do you remember that part of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When Nenad Santic ordered your son to hand over the gun, did you think of any position which Nenad Santic held? Did he hold some position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was their chief commander, and his sister was also in the HVO, that is Slavica, Nenad's sister. She is still in the HVO and she is Drago Josipovic's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So Nenad Santic was in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was their commander. He was the one to be asked and he was ordering everything, what was going to be done in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic, was he in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a soldier. He always wore the camouflage uniform and always a rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Ahmic, we have concluded. You are very courageous and the Tribunal thanks you. You came all this way to us to explain in your own words what you experienced. Registrar, could we have Ms. Ahmic escorted from the courtroom? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, until 1.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the next witness we have is Haris Hrnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You can have him brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please give me your family name and your first name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Haris Hrnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are going to give you a declaration and we will ask you to read it while you are still standing, after which you may sit down. MR. HARIS HRNJIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. The Prosecutor has asked you to come to testify here as part of the trial against General Blaskic who is here as well. The Prosecutor will ask you the questions which he feels are appropriate, after which General Blaskic's Defence counsel will also ask you questions, as will the judges, if they feel so inclined. Mr. Kehoe, we have ten minutes. I would ask you to begin and then we will resume in the afternoon. Please have him spell his name, because I did not really quite get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I will. Haris, before we begin, could you spell your name for the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: H-R-N-J-I-C H-A-R-I-S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Haris, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20, I will be 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When the events took place in April 1993, how old were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was 16 and I was going to be 17 that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, tell the judges a little bit about your family, your father's name, your mother's name, your brother's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father's name was Mehmed Hrnjic, he was born in 1945. My mother is Samija, she was born in 1948. My brother, his name was Admir Hrnjic and he was born in 1969, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How old was your brother Admir in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, in April 1993, what village did you live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How long had your family lived in the village of Santici before April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About eight years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before that, where did you and your family live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before we moved to Santici, we lived in Zenica in the neighbourhood called Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why did you move from Zenica to Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lived close to the steel mills in Zenica and so the air was very polluted. That is why we moved to Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did your family open up a business when you got to Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my father first opened a restaurant and after that, he also opened a shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This building where the shop and the restaurant were, did your family live in the same building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I lived in the same building, in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to the first conflict. Do you remember the first conflict in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it, the first conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You and your family were living in Santici at the time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why did the conflict break out in Santici in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly why it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, I am talking about when. When approximately did the first conflict break out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 18th October, around 18th October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell the judges what happened, Haris.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, around 6.00, I heard shooting coming from various weapons. Outside my brother and I got up and went to our parents' bedroom and my brother said that there was shooting going on and the father said that he heard it and that we should pull back into the hallway of the house. We sat there and we took the telephone with us. We stayed there, I entered into one of the rooms and went to the window and saw the HVO soldiers running through my yard, and I saw one soldier running on the road towards Pican's cafe. After that, I saw Nenad Santic going from his house in the direction of their command, the HVO command. After that, I saw Nenad Santic approaching with a truck which had an anti-aircraft gun mounted on it, and he was in this truck and this truck was going in the direction of Ahmici. The truck passed houses and then I did not see it any more. Then I heard shooting, heavy, and after that the truck came back and came to a stop at the parking area in front of my house. Nenad Santic then trained a gun towards our house and then Ivo Vidovic came and Anto Vidovic with him. They were talking to Nenad about something, and then the truck went to and parked in front of Ivo Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second, Haris. Who was Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nenad Santic was a commander of the HVO in Santici, in the Santici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was he a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was, a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You and your family were Muslims, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that after he had been spoken to by Ivo Vidovic they pulled the anti-aircraft weapon away, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is 1.00, I am going to move to another date after this, so it would be an appropriate time to end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We will resume at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing. Please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Haris Hrnjic, did you rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have rested, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We had begun with the examination, you are a Prosecution witness. Mr. Kehoe, you may resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Haris, before the lunch break we ended at 18th October 1992, when you were describing Nenad Santic in possession of an anti-aircraft weapon. After the 18th, did your father have additional contact with Nenad Santic, and did he ask Nenad Santic to -- did Nenad Santic tell your father to come to the HVO headquarters in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was -- first they came to search the house. Nenad Santic was there, Zeljko, I do not know his last name and Miro Josipovic. They searched the house and after that, they called my father to go with them to the HVO command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened to your father at the HVO command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A pistol was found in the house, for which there was a permit too, so this was taken away, and Nenad Santic threatened my father. Zeljko gave him some kind of a certificate that this weapon was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After that particular incident, did your family have additional problems with members of the HVO at the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the 23rd at night we heard shooting in front of the house. My family was there, and I was watching through the window. I saw an HVO van and in the front, in black lettering, it was written, "HVO", and I saw a soldier in the middle of our parking area, and another one was over off to the side next to our house, one of them was shooting in the air. I pulled back, I heard the glass shattering. This was in our store. A little bit later, we could hear the engines start and a van pulled out and then it stopped again. After that, there were two powerful explosions. My father, since Nenad Santic had told him if there were any problems that he should call him on the telephone, that he would come; my father called him up and after about 15 minutes he arrived at our house. We came downstairs and we saw that the glass, the windows of the store were shattered, that some things were taken away and you could see where the grenades -- they were hand grenades, you could see where they had fallen. Nenad Santic arrived in a car and said that he was going in the direction of Vitez, where the van had gone, so that he would check to see who was in this van. Then Ivo Vidovic came, an older man. They both had the HVO uniforms on and carried weapons and were standing guard there, of sorts. Later, Nenad Santic returned and told us that he could not find the van and that the HVO soldiers who were at the barricade not far from our house, that they were asleep when he arrived there and that they did not see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, you said this was the 23rd and you are talking about 23rd October 1992, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No HVO soldiers were ever arrested for destroying the restaurant, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody was ever arrested and nobody ever came on the part of the HVO, only Nenad Santic came, that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did this instil fear in you and the other members of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it did instil fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Around this time in October 1992, did you see Dario Kordic in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Dario Kordic in front of my house. He was in a car, I do not know the make, and I saw Nenad Santic and Slavica Josipovic. They then entered the car with him and left. Later I saw them on TV Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You saw Dario Kordic with Nenad Santic and then you said you later saw who on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dario Kordic and Slavica Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you also see Dario Kordic on television with the defendant Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Between October 1992 and April 1993, did you and members of your family, or did members of your family continue to receive threatening phone calls because you were Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they constantly called us on the phone, they talked in a provocative way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, at this point we are going to move to 16th April 1993, but before we do that, with, Mr. President, and your Honours, with your permission, I would just like to hand the witness what has been marked for identification as 129A, and also a legend that goes with it that has been marked 129B. I would also ask if we could, with the assistance of the usher, put 129A, the legend, on the ELMO. . They have been premarked, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What was marked? I think we saw this already, but there is a legend here which does not perhaps correspond to the other numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this particular exhibit is an enlargement of portions of Exhibit 50. However, the markings on them, in this particular case, 1 through 15, are unique. They are markings designed to correspond to Mr. Hrnjic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore the legend would have a specific number, is that correct? Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, this is a new exhibit, the map is 129A and the legend is 129B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, before we begin to talk about what happened on the morning of 16th April, could you use the pointer and point to the place where you lived and where the shop and the restaurant was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What number is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, in order to speed things up a bit, if what you intend to do is to designate with a pointer all of the numbers that appear on the map, I think it would be simpler to ask the witness, without interrupting, to indicate to us all the numbers, unless that is not your intention, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is perfectly fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. I would speak directly to the witness. One after the other, from 1 to 15, you would indicate without being interrupted all the houses that you recognise and the sites that you recognise. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please say "number 1 is my house, number 2 is the house of", et cetera. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 1, that is my house. Number 2 is the house of Pican, it is Pican's cafe. Number 3 is Ivo Vidovic's house. Number 4 is the Colic house, that is where the HVO command was. Number 5 is the house of Mustafa Mujo Dedic. Number 6 is the garage of Mujo Dedic. Number 7 is Islam Ahmic's house. Number 8 is the house of Munib Ribo. Number 9 is the house of Nesib Ahmic. Number 10 is the house of Heleg. Number 11 is the Ramiz Ahmic's house, number 12 is Sefik Ahmic's house, number 13 is Adem Siljak's house, number 14 is Hasan's house, number 15 is Ivica Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Under those conditions, you can now ask the questions which would allow you to specify or to clarify certain points that you wish clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, let us go to the morning of 16th April 1993. Can you tell the judges what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 5.00 or 6.00, we heard a powerful explosion. My brother and I woke up, we went to our parents' bedroom, our parents were awake and the brother said that we heard a powerful explosion, and my father said that he had heard it too and then we all moved to the hallway, the whole family did. We were there in the hallway and then my uncle called us from Zenica, from the Tetovo neighbourhood. He had heard the explosion and he asked us whether it was there where we were and we said it was, and he told us to just remain there, because he remembered that during the first attack we stayed in the hallway, so we stayed in the hallway. My brother wanted to take something from our room, and when he opened the door the shooting started at the house itself, the glass started shattering. The shots came from the direction of Ivo Vidovic's house and the house of Anto Vidosevic. My brother pulled back into the hallway and we went and stayed under a staircase. At that point, we heard the voices saying, "boss, boss, come out of the house". My father opened the entrance door, he put his hands up and he said that we were surrendering, that we were not armed. There were two HVO soldiers there. They took us out outside. There was another house across and they told us to go and look at the house and we should not turn around and look at our house. Then they entered our house, but there was a dog there, and he started for them and they killed it. After they killed it, they entered the house. When they brought us to this fence in front of the Pican's cafe, there were several members of the HVO there. They told them, "shoot", we turn around that we should be shot on the spot. They went in and they were banging around the house and they said, "if we find any weapons, we will cut your throats". They were searching, they did not find anything, they only found a box where the pistol was, that was the pistol Nenad Santic had taken. They asked where this pistol was, my father said that Nenad Santic had taken this pistol and then they were silent. Then they called my father into the house and he stayed there for about five minutes. When he returned, he told us that they had taken his wallet. Then they again ransacked the house and came out without finding anything. When they came out, one of them was carrying a gas can that was from our own house and they asked the soldiers in front of Pican's cafe, "what shall we do with them?". One of them said, "take them to where all the rest of them are". Then they ordered us to start going in the direction of Vitez, and we did, we put our hands on our heads as we were passing the HVO soldiers who were in front of the Pican's cafe. They were laughing at us, they were making comments, and then told us to move faster; we did. We came to Mujo Dedic's house --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second, Haris. If we can go back to the ELMO for a moment, originally you said that -- earlier you said that the shooting in the morning started in front of Ivo Vidovic's house. Would that have been right in front of the house circled with number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that soldiers came to the front of your house number 1. Can you describe those soldiers to the judges? What were they wearing, insignias, were their faces painted or covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were soldiers in camouflage uniforms. One of them had a helmet, we were not allowed to look at them, I could not see any insignia. They had paint on their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But they had camouflage uniforms on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had camouflage uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You previously designated number 2 as Pican's cafe and you said that there were soldiers standing in front of Pican's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is Pican's cafe, that is marked with number 2 and the HVO soldiers were in front of Pican's cafe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In order to avoid repeating this, we are going to run into the problem of having the confusion of all kinds of methods at the same time. He will say what he has to say. I think in his statement he said that he did identify the cafe. I know that you are thinking about the transcript, but in the transcript he did say that that would be number 2, because we have the legend here. Let us try to save some time here, because I do feel we are going to go back again over the narrative and ask the witness to repeat everything he has said, and asking him to clarify things by saying "this is number 1, this is number 2". We have to go forward, Mr. Kehoe. Go ahead, please. Do not be afraid, please. It is in the transcript, it is all right. We have Pican's cafe there, it is number 2, the judges understood that. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. How many soldiers were in front of Pican's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms and they all had their faces painted, except for one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you recognise that one who did not have his face painted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that you left that area and were headed towards the house of Mujo Dedic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is number 5 on the chart. Tell the judges what happened there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you wish to say it, say it, but let us not repeat things, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, Haris.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two members of the HVO took us to Mujo Dedic's house. When we arrived at the house, it was on fire, and there I saw the bodies of Munib Ribo and Mujo Dedic, they were killed. When we came there, they told us to stop there. We did. Then they ordered me and my mum and my brother to start towards the garage. We did that. Then they ordered my brother to open up the garage and to lock us inside and to come back to where my father was, to that place. When they locked me up in the garage, I heard shots after a while. When I peeked through the door of the garage, I saw the bodies of my father and brother lying there, they were dead, they were killed. We stayed there and then the HVO members left this place and left us behind. There were a lot of people there in a small room, we did not have food or water. Then around 5.00, three HVO members arrived, one of them had a mask of sorts. We recognised him though, that is Ivica Semren, his nickname was Zuti, which means "blond". Drazenko Vidovic came and a third soldier whom I did not know. They took us from -- from that room, they took us to Nesib Ahmic's -- from the garage of Mujo Dedic, they took us to the house of Hasim Dedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you before you move on to the garage of Nesib Ahmic. You said that when you were walking up to the garage there were two men who were already dead, Mujo Dedic and Ribo Munib?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were those two men Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that you stayed in the garage until later on in the afternoon and more HVO soldiers came. When those HVO soldiers came, did any of the soldiers ask anybody in the garage to come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they wanted to take out Haris Dedic, he was called out by the third HVO member whom we did not know. He said that he would not come out because he was afraid that he would be killed just like they had killed his brother and father. Then Drazenko Vidovic said to let him be, that he was only 13 years old, that he was still a child. Then this HVO member did not call him out after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So Haris Dedic's father and brother were also killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the way to Nesib Ahmic's house from the garage of Mujo Dedic, did you see any other dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the body of Islam Ahmic in the yard of his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Islam Ahmic also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the -- by the way, who took you to the house of Nesib Ahmic, how many soldiers and describe what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms, and it was those three members, those three soldiers who had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then you went to Nesib Ahmic's house. Had that house been burnt as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the house was also set on fire, but only the lower floor was burnt and the attic had remained unburnt, so they took us up there, to the attic and we were there, it was very hot and we did not have any water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, at this point you said that Nesib Ahmic's house had been burnt. Were the rest of the Muslim houses in that area that are depicted on the map 129A, were they all burning as well or had they been burnt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the house of Hasan was not burning. All the other houses were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were all the other houses that were on fire, were they owned by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was only Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that Hasan's house, number 14 on the chart, was not burning that morning, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But was it burnt thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was burnt thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That morning, was Hasan at home or was he abroad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Hasan was not at home that morning, he was away, he was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in every other house where there was a man present, a Muslim man present, that house was burnt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every house was burning where there was such a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that you went to Nesib Ahmic's house. What happened when you went to Nesib Ahmic's house and where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came do his house, we were taken to the attic and we spent the night there. In the morning soldiers came, but they had yellow patches here (indicates), and they told us that we were to be exchanged from Nesib Ahmic's house. They took us to the HVO command, to the Colic house. When we came there, there were other people there, Muslims, who were prisoners and we were sitting there, we were guarded by Anto Papic there, and I was with Heleg then, and he told me that if anything happened to him I should know that he gathered dead bodies near Ramiz Ahmic's house, and if anything happened to him, that I should tell his son that Nenad Santic is to be blamed for all of this that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, let me stop you for a second. Can I show you a photograph, with the assistance of the usher and the Registrar, Exhibit 121/2 that has been received in evidence. If we could place that on the ELMO, please? Haris, is that the man that you know as Heleg that you were talking to at Colic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is Heleg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What did he tell you about collecting bodies before he went to collect bodies on this occasion? What did he tell you he had previously done that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that he was collecting bodies and that he brought them into the yard of Ramiz Ahmic, by his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is number 11 on the chart, your Honours. What happened after that? You went in there, had this conversation with Heleg, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After some time, two members of the HVO walked into the room, and they started choosing people who would go and collect dead bodies. They chose Heleg, Zenur Ahmic, Amir Ahmic and Hasim Ahmic. They wanted to take Haris Dedic too, but his mother got up and cried and she said that they had killed her son and her husband and they should spare him. After that, Nikica Plavcic, called Slikica, walked into the room. The women asked where these people who were taken away were and he said that their special units had killed these people and that they would not be coming back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Killed who, Haris?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They killed Heleg, Ahmic Zenur, Amir Ahmic and Hasim Ahmic. Also he told us that they were going to a place called Pirici, that they would go there to burn and kill as they did in Ahmici, their special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who did Nikica say was going to do this? Who did he say was going to go to Pirici and kill and burn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The members of the HVO, these special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This was on 17th April, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You lived through this, Haris. You heard Nikica talk about special forces doing this in Pirici. Did these soldiers operate together with your Croat neighbours in Santici to commit these crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did it with the help of our neighbours, and our neighbours did the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Without the help of a village, would you be able to distinguish a Muslim house from a Croat house in the village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, you could not tell the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Muslim houses, allegedly, have a four sided roof and Croat houses have two sided roofs. My house has a two sided roof and Pican has a four sided roof, so that shows that they could not tell, somebody had to take them round and show them the houses and do it with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we go back to 129A, please? If we can put that on the ELMO? Haris, just pointing to this, number 2 is Pican's cafe with a four sided roof.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Pican's cafe with the four sided roof, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that owned by a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a Croat house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was it destroyed on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not even damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move to number 15. Do you see number 15 a little further up on the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that a four sided or a two sided house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four sided roof. It is a Croat house, and it was not destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that Josip Vidovic or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Josip Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said previously that your house was a two sided house. Take a look, for example, at numbers 12, 13 and 14. Were they two sided roofs or four sided roofs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are two sided roofs there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And those houses belong to Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These houses belong to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you conclude prior to this attack that the people that were attacking knew who lived -- what Muslims lived in what houses and what Croats lived in what houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they knew which houses were Muslim houses and which houses were Croat houses. Look at the map. Not a single Croat house was damaged and all the other Muslim houses were burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After the four individuals -- we are done with the ELMO now, thank you, Mr. Usher. After this conversation with Nikica concerning the special forces taking these individuals out to be killed and that they were going to go to Pirici, did you ever see any of these four men again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never saw these four people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened after that? Continue on with the story and tell the judges what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, we were locked up in this HVO command. Then two UN transport vehicles came, personnel carriers, women with babies went out and asked for help. Then Ivica Vidovic ran from his house, waving to the UNPROFOR soldiers, then he walked up to them, they talked for a while, he went into the personnel carrier and he took them to his house. After that, we were locked up in there and then Plavcic Nikica, called Slikica, came and told us he was taking us to be exchanged. He took us all towards Vitez. We reached a place called Dubravica. We stopped there, then they asked whether they should take us to the school in Vitez or whether they should take us to the elementary school there in Dubravica. After a while, Franjo Krizanac came up, he was a friend of Islam Ahmic, and he came to get Islam Ahmic's wife. He asked about Islam and he was told that he was killed. Then he took Mijda Ahmic, Amil Ahmic, Elmir Ahmic and me, he took them into his car and Ahmic Mirza. Then he took us to Vitez, to the apartment of Dajic Sulejman. We spent 17 days there. After that, Franjo Krizanac took us to the elementary school, he registered us with the Red Cross, that we were to be exchanged, but that was not the way it happened. It was not the Red Cross there, I do not know what was there, so then he took us to the road to Zenica, the road that went around but that led to Zenica. Then he left us there and he said that we should go towards Zenica that way, but he could not help us any further, so we set out along this mountain road towards Zenica. When we took the road, we saw HVO soldiers at the Muslim cemetery. There was a fence there, so they got into the Muslim cemetery and they had set up a line there and the Armija was on the other side, so we went through all of that and the Croat soldiers were drinking water. As we were passing by, a sniper started shooting at us, we had to lie down on the ground, and then we continued afterwards and we found refuge in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Haris, Franjo Krizanac was a Croat, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he try to help you and the other Muslims that he took into the apartment in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may turn to the last and final exhibit, Mr. President, I believe it is 130, I do not think there is going to be any problem going through these photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are these personal photos? I would like to ask a question of the witness, if you permit me to. Mr. Haris, Hrnjic, these are personal photos, family pictures, is that what these are?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, they are family photographs and a neighbour's photograph who was murdered at the time, on the day that Ribo Munib --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I am turning to Haris Hrnjic. We are going to show you some photographs of people you know. Do you agree to see them? If you do not want to see them, we do not have to look at them. Are you strong enough to look at these pictures to identify them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if we can take those out? If we can go to the first photograph, Haris, is that your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my family and friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: About when was this picture taken and where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photograph was taken in 1989, in 1990, in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was this when your brother was in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was doing his service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you pick out your family on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. This is my father, Mehmed Hrnjic. This is me. This is my brother, Admir Hrnjic, and this is my mummy, Samija Hrnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go quickly, please. We have already said it this morning, these are photographs that cause a great deal of suffering. Does the Defence have any intention of contesting these photographs? Mr. Hayman, do you have any intention of contesting these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of course not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will identify these photographs and then the witness will agree with what the photographs are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to say something. You are going to go through the pictures quickly and say if you recognise -- these are photographs of people you were very close to, your relatives, you will say yes, they will be put in as exhibits, the Defence does not intend to challenge them and we will try to mitigate the witness's suffering. Let us go very quickly, please. Haris, would you go through this album very quickly so that -- we have all seen them, go through them very quickly, you have it in front of you, and just tell us if you recognise all the photographs. Do it quickly, go ahead. Try to be strong, it will be over in a few moments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my brother Admir Hrnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The next one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Munib Ribo with his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The next one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Ribo Munib with his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you are very brave. The Defence is not going to challenge these, these will be entered as what number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be 130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Kehoe, you can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, just to clarify, the second picture is his brother, 130/2, and the last two photographs are 130/3 and 4, which are Ribo Munib. I have just clarified so we have it sequentially. Mr. President, your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Haris, you will now be questioned by either the attorney or attorneys of General Blaskic. This is a Tribunal. The accused is presumed to be innocent, he has defenders and now you must answer their questions. Do not be afraid at all, the judges are here and I believe it will be Mr. Nobilo, is Mr. Nobilo going to do it? Very well, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Haris, I am Anto Nobilo, attorney for General Blaskic. This is my colleague Russell Hayman. He is also an attorney of General Blaskic. I only have a few questions for you. When that explosion occurred in the shop downstairs, when those grenades were thrown when Santic was there, the next day, did you report that incident to the police station in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, you said that in house number 4, there was a command. What command was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The command of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For what area, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the area of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that a private house, did somebody live there before, or was the command there only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Downstairs in the house was the HVO command and upstairs the Colic family had their living quarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the soldiers came, somebody called out to your father saying "boss, boss"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you recognise the voice or did you know who called your father that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think I do not know. A lot of people called my father "boss", he had these shops there, you know. But I did not recognise the voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did somebody steal 29,000 Deutsch Marks from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 16th April 1993, when my father was called into the house and they took my father's wallet and money away. He told me that, he told us that when he came back, he told my family about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you went towards Mujo Dedic's house, can you tell me what time it was, what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were going to Mujo Dedic's house, it was about 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it true that at the Colic house, Anto Papic said, "I will take care of you and nobody will kill you"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that what you told the investigators before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You did not? Thank you. Do you know Bruno Santic, the son of Nenad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bruno Santic is the son of Zvonko Santic, not Nenad Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he have insignia of the Croat army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did have insignia of the army of Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where does he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Donje Rovine, near Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What unit did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the special unit of Dario Kordic, in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you ever see our client on television, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you hear what he said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not hear anything, I just saw him with Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You never paid attention to his words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not listen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 16th or 17th April 1993 in Santici, did you perhaps see Blaskic in Santici, or did you ever see Blaskic in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said that I only saw Dario Kordic, not Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In Santici then, on 16th and 17th, did anybody mention General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear anyone mention him because I did not dare listen a lot. I did not even dare watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, we have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You said in response to cross-examination that Bruno Santic was a member of a special unit of Dario Kordic. Do you recall being asked that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Bruno Santic told you this prior to the first conflict in October 1992, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I failed to introduce or offer into evidence Exhibit 129A and B. If I failed to do so, I do so now. I know, Mr. President, you accepted into evidence 130, but I offer it if I have not done so. I have no further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objection from the Defence? Then Registrar, this will be put under that number. No other questions, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It will soon be over, Haris. I turn to my colleagues, perhaps they have some questions. Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You mentioned that the HVO could not have found the houses of the Muslims by themselves, they had to have the help of the Croat inhabitants of the village; was that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They must have helped them, the villagers, because they were also in the HVO, most of them were, and they did help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there, in your opinion, a reason for the people of the village to hate the Muslims and what provoked this hatred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what provoked it. When I came home on 15th April, I came back from the school, and everything was normal. I prepared everything for 16th April. We were together all the time, we were neighbours, but in the morning, the attack occurred and I do not know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you notice any propaganda which conditioned the Croat inhabitants against the Muslims, or were you too young to notice that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the first conflict, the situation deteriorated, because then they threatened my family, they were targeting the house and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that particular to your house, or was it a general attitude?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it concerned all the Muslims. After the first conflict, it just seemed that they did not want us to live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You mentioned that in front of the Pican's cafe the HVO soldiers asked that everybody would be shot, to shoot on the spot. Did they do the shooting, or was it just talking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They just talked about taking us to where everybody else was taken, and the two who came in front of the house, and who had taken us over there, they shot my father and my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They were HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Somebody said, "Nenad Santic is to be responsible for anything happening". What was the role of Nenad Santic? Was he a commander in the HVO, was he a soldier? Why was he responsible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the HVO commander in Santici and he was the one who worked the most against us Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen is going to ask a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Haris, you went to school on 15th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where was the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My school was in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There were Croat pupils in school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a school like everywhere else, so all ethnic groups were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you have friends amongst the Croat pupils at school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you came back from school on the afternoon of 15th April, did you then expect to go back to school on the 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I expected that and I prepared my things to go back to school on the 16th, books and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take it that you expected to see your Croat friends at school on 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I assumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Haris, it is over now. I would like to ask you what you do now. At the time you were 16, now you are 21, what do you do, how do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am doing my regular military service in the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Meanwhile, I graduated from the secondary school for machine workers in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have nothing else to ask you. Would you like to add something that you did not have the chance to say in response to the questions that were asked of you? Do you have anything that you would like to ask? Have you said everything that you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said everything that I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Tribunal thanks you. It took a great deal of courage to come and say all that you did. We have completed what we have to do here, we can ask the usher to have the witness escorted from the courtroom before the next one comes in. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Registrar has just told me this is a protected witness, I am saying this for the public gallery, but it is not an in camera session. We are going to lower the blinds and take a few minutes to bring in the next witness. Then once the protective measures have been set up, we will raise the blinds again so that the testimony can begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We were informed at lunch-time that there was another concern, a medical concern regarding this witness. At the time that we came into the courtroom at 2.30, she was not here. We do not know what her status is right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We will suspend the hearing for ten minutes or fifteen minutes and then we can be informed what will be taking place next. We will suspend the hearing for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing, please be seated. Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. We are ready to proceed with the next witness who is a protected witness and will be identified as Witness I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness I, we will first verify your identity, but you do not state your name. The Registrar is going to show you -- do you hear me, first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Registrar is going to show you a piece of paper with your name on it. That is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now ask you to make a declaration. Please relax, you are before judges, try to be calm. The Registrar is going to read you -- it is not a long oath, the Registrar will read it to you and you will repeat after him. Please speak slowly, Mr. Registrar. WITNESS I (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You have nothing to fear, Witness I. You have come at the request of the Prosecutor, he will begin to ask you questions. Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness I, I would like you to relax while I ask you these questions. It is okay if you turn your head in my direction and turn your head back toward the judges. You do not have to sit as rigidly as you are at the moment. Please make yourself comfortable and feel at ease before I start asking you these questions. Witness I, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where were you born and raised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Karaula and I grew up in Karaula, near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Karaula, approximately 7 kilometres away from Turbe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You had four years of education, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness I, when did you move to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I moved in 1992 on 19th November.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you explain to the judges why you moved to Ahmici on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, we got away from the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Had they been attacking your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As a result of that, did you become a refugee and move to the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you reside in Ahmici with your late husband and your two children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was a refugee.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you lived in Ahmici, did you live there with members of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who were those, without identifying them by name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was me, my husband and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In April 1993, how old was your late husband?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In April 1993, how old were your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was 19, the other one 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I believe the oldest child was a girl and the youngest was a boy, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness I, are you relaxed in that chair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. When you went to Ahmici, did you occupy the bottom floor of a house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did a Muslim man occupy the top floor of the house? Please do not identify his name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that Muslim man your landlord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How old was your landlord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 48 to 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was the house that you lived in in Ahmici in the part of Ahmici known as lower Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lower Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How far away were you, that house, located from the lower mosque in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Looking out of your window from the house that you, your husband and two children occupied, what could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see when they killed the son of Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before we get to that particular part of your testimony, from your house, could you see the Catholic cemetery and could you see a large field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn briefly and ask you some questions about your late husband. While you were living in the village of Ahmici, was your late husband a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Territorial Defence in your former village of Karaula, or did he also continue his duties as a member of the Territorial Defence in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in Karaula but not down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So he was not a member of the Territorial Defence in the village of Ahmici in April 1993, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did your husband ever go out and participate in village guard duties while he was in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On 16th April 1993, were there any weapons in the part of the house that you, your husband and two children occupied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Witness I, were there any weapons in the part of the house that was occupied by your landlord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn, if I could, to 16th April 1993. First of all, was your husband and were your two children also present in the house on that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was the landlord upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please tell the judges what happened on the morning of April 16th 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April 1993, I heard shooting around 5.50. I got up, I yelled and rose my husband and my children. I said that we should run if we could. When we went to the hole and opened the window, we saw that it was not our own army. Then we withdrew to the room, we stayed there. Then I stopped talking, then there was a burst of fire and some crying. Then we came out again, and again wanted to run, but we could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness I, let me interrupt you for just a minute. When you looked out the window, you said you saw some soldiers. Can you describe those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I looked through the window, we wanted to get out and then they killed Husein Ahmic at that time. We saw we could not get out and we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you identify any of those soldiers or could you describe what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know them, but they were all in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were their faces covered or partially covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two had their faces covered and two did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you looked out of the window, did you see Husein Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Tell the judges how old Husein Ahmic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately over 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How was he dressed on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just regular, a pair of pants and some sweater.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you saw Husein Ahmic, did he have any weapons with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you saw Husein Ahmic, where was he in relation to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in front of his house and then they killed him and then they pulled him around behind the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you actually see these soldiers kill Husein Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At the time you saw the soldiers kill Husein Ahmic, was his house on fire or was it not on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: After you saw Husein Ahmic killed, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that we could not get out, so we withdrew to the room, the four of us. We sat down, I put some foam in the windows and then I heard more shooting and some crying, and I heard them to our house, they immediately shattered the window and the glass came over us, and my daughter said, "let us get out because they will throw in a grenade". No sooner did we leave the room than the hand grenade was lobbed in and it exploded in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you do after the grenade exploded in the room where you, your husband and two children had been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
